transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-30
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jessie Morales (Redwood SE), Maya Lin (CitrineWorks), Omar Reyes (Platform Lead), Claire Bennett (Security)

Summary (auto):
CitrineWorks evaluating integration path for Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Primary concerns: SDK support for LangChain/LlamaIndex, running through an internal gateway/proxy, rate-limiting headers, observability hooks (traces/metrics), and security (SAML/KMS). Agreed next steps: bench on Dedicated trial, share security pack, proposal + SOW.

Topics: SDK compatibility; gateway/proxy sidecar vs direct calls; rate limits and token quotas; observability / OpenTelemetry traces; pilot success criteria; timeline and procurement touch points.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir from Redwood, AE, joined by Jessie on the technical side. How are you all?
[00:05] Maya: Good, thanks. Maya here. We're dialed in — Omar and Claire are with me.
[00:09] Omar: Hey team.
[00:11] Claire: Hi.
[00:14] Samir: Cool. Quick agenda: do a short run through of where you are, integration patterns you care about, then Jessie will dig into SDK/gateway specifics and we can capture next steps.
[00:22] Maya: Sounds good. High level: CitrineWorks runs an internal inference gateway that routes LLM calls from our services. We want to understand whether we should talk to Redwood Hosted directly from services, or route through our gateway (sidecar/proxy). Also LangChain and LlamaIndex are in our stack.
[00:36] Jessie: Great. To call out upfront, Redwood's SDKs are idiomatic for JS/Python and we have first-class connectors/examples for LangChain and LlamaIndex. There's a client + streaming support; and we expose headers for quotas and a tracing hook for OTEL.
[00:50] Omar: On the gateway: we have strict egress controls, so ideally the gateway handles auth and we do internal calls to gateway. Will Redwood accept proxied requests where the original user identity is preserved in headers?
[01:03] Jessie: Yes, you can use a gateway or sidecar. For hosted deployments we generally expect the token in the outbound call, but many customers forward a service-to-service token and include X-Forwarded-User or a customer-defined header. We do recommend using mutual TLS on the gateway-egress side for extra security when connecting to Dedicated or Private.
[01:22] Claire: For security, we need SOC2 docs, encryption at rest, KMS integration, and audit logs. Can Redwood support our KMS and provide per-tenant audit trails?
[01:33] Samir: Short answer: yes. We integrate with major KMS providers for Private and Dedicated; Hosted has managed keys but BYOK on Dedicated/Private. Audit logs with token-level granularity are available via the Console; we can share sample exports. We'll follow up with the security pack.
[01:47] Maya: Perfect. On SDKs, we use LangChain chains heavily. Does Redwood's SDK include a LangChain adapter or do we maintain our own adapter?
[01:56] Jessie: We have maintained examples for LangChain prompts and conversation chains, and a small adapter module for LlamaIndex doc loaders. The adapter is intentionally lightweight. For production we recommend pinning a model-version and using our long-lived API key or issuing short-lived JWTs from your gateway.
[02:12] Omar: What's the story about rate limits? We have bursty traffic and need predictable quotas — can we do per-team or per-route quotas?
[02:20] Samir: Yes, Redwood supports per-token quota and per-route quotas at the account level for Hosted; for Dedicated you get configurable capacity reservations and soft/hard rate caps. You can set route-level rate limiting in the Console and inject X-Rate-Limit headers back to your gateway.
[02:35] Claire: Are those headers standard? Like X-RateLimit-Remaining?
[02:38] Jessie: We emit X-Rate-Limit-Limit, X-Rate-Limit-Remaining, and X-Rate-Limit-Reset by default. For Dedicated/Private you can customize header names via the routing layer.
[02:48] Maya: Nice. How about batching and latency — we have low-latency interactive UI requirements, p95 under 300ms for short prompts, but batch jobs can take longer.
[02:58] Jessie: That's a common pattern. For interactive, we suggest small batch sizes, prefix cache, and streaming — that reduces p95. Dedicated gives you the predictable throughput to keep p95 low. Hosted can hit those numbers but depends on tenancy; we recommend a Dedicated trial if you need consistent p95 SLAs.
[03:15] Omar: Can you elaborate on prefix caching — is it client-side or server-side?
[03:18] Jessie: We do both. Our runtime supports automatic KV cache for prefix tokens server-side when you pin a model version and enable caching. On the client side you can also cache embeddings and reuse session keys. We can share the cache TTL recommendations.
[03:33] Maya: For LlamaIndex, we rely on chunked embeddings and a custom retriever. Any guidance on connecting the retriever to Redwood so embeddings are stored/served efficiently?
[03:42] Jessie: Two approaches: 1) Use our embeddings API directly and store vectors in your vector DB; 2) If you want lower latency, run local embedding sidecars or use Dedicated with colocated vector store. We have an example for LlamaIndex that shows using Redwood embeddings + external Milvus/Weaviate.
[03:59] Claire: Observability — we run OpenTelemetry traces across services. Can Redwood ingest trace ids and correlate inference spans?
[04:07] Jessie: Yes, we accept traceparent / tracestate headers and emit spans in your trace backend if you wire our OTEL exporter. For Hosted we provide a hosted tracing hook that forwards anonymized trace metadata; for Dedicated/Private you can run the exporter in your VPC and get full fidelity.
[04:25] Omar: Any limits on headers size when proxying? Our gateway injects a bunch of metadata.
[04:31] Jessie: Large headers can hit edge limits; we recommend keeping header payloads under 8KB. For heavy metadata, pass a reference id and push full metadata to a side-channel like S3 or internal metadata service.
[04:45] Maya: Good note. On auth: we use SAML SSO and also issue short-lived OIDC tokens to services. Can Redwood accept OIDC tokens minted by our OIDC provider?
[04:55] Samir: Yes, supported. For Hosted we can integrate via OIDC/OAuth flows; for Dedicated/Private it's straightforward to accept your tokens and map claims to RBAC. We also support service account keys and rotation via our API.
[05:09] Claire: Data residency — some of our models touch EU customer data. Can we restrict model serving in eu-west regions only?
[05:17] Samir: Absolutely. Dedicated and Private allow strict region pinning. Hosted can be region-constrained depending on account; we can reserve capacity in eu-west for your workloads.
[05:25] Omar: Let's talk about proxies: sidecar vs centralized proxy — pros/cons from Redwood's perspective?
[05:31] Jessie: Sidecar gives you lower intra-service latency and better per-request telemetry since it's local to the service. Central proxy is simpler for egress control and policy enforcement. With Redwood you can do either; for sidecar we provide a lightweight SDK and a sidecar image. For central proxy, we recommend using our routing headers and preserving trace ids.
[05:52] Maya: If we use a proxy, do we need to transform payloads for streaming? We've had trouble getting bidirectional streaming through our gateway.
[05:59] Jessie: Streaming through proxies depends on the proxy's support for chunked transfer. If your proxy supports HTTP/1.1 chunked or HTTP/2 with streaming, it will work. Otherwise we fallback to polling or websockets. We can help test your proxy.
[06:15] Claire: From a compliance side, we need to know retention policies for logs and prompts. Can we opt-out of prompt logging for Hosted?
[06:23] Samir: Hosted by default retains logs for debugging, but there is a data-retention control and an opt-out or redaction pipeline for sensitive data. Dedicated/Private give you full control — you can disable prompt retention entirely. We'll surface the retention settings in the Console and in the security pack.
[06:40] Omar: Pricing — rough banding for Dedicated and pilot?
[06:44] Samir: We'll put precise numbers in the SOW. Roughly Dedicated is a committed monthly for GPU pools plus per-token accounting for overage. Pilot options: short-term Dedicated trial with a capped usage band we can agree on.
[06:58] Maya: Pilot success criteria — we want to validate: 1) p95 latency under 300ms for regional traffic, 2) <2% error rate under 1k concurrent users, 3) integration with LangChain & LlamaIndex without SDK changes beyond config. Is that reasonable?
[07:15] Jessie: Yes, that's reasonable. We'll run the bench and provide p50/p95/p99 numbers and error breakdown with and without caching.
[07:25] Claire: Who will run the bench? We prefer Redwood SE to run a simulated load against our Dedicated trial to remove network variability on our side.
[07:33] Jessie: We can run from our test tenants but recommend running from your network to capture egress and VPC effects. That said, we can do a dual-run: our bench for baseline, your bench for final acceptance.
[07:48] Omar: Do you have any known issues with LlamaIndex connectors? We've seen tokenization mismatches before.
[07:54] Jessie: Some connectors assume a particular tokenizer and chunk size; our examples default to UTF-8 tokenization and recommend aligning chunk sizes. We'll share LlamaIndex example code and a checklist for tokenization.
[08:09] Maya: On observability hooks, can we get raw inference metrics back (latency per model, tokens-in/out, failed requests) into Datadog?
[08:18] Jessie: Yes, you can push metrics via our Datadog exporter or pull from the Console API. We export per-route metrics, token counts, and error codes. For Dedicated, you can also stream raw telemetry to your SIEM.
[08:32] Claire: About RBAC — can we map SAML groups to Redwood roles?
[08:38] Samir: Yes. SAML or OIDC claims mapping to roles is supported. We'll work with your identity team to map groups to RBAC policies.
[08:47] Omar: Any constraints on model size or quantization for Dedicated? We plan to load quantized models for cost reasons.
[08:55] Jessie: Dedicated supports quantized runtimes; we have recommended quant profiles and can recommend kernels depending on your GPU. If you're bringing custom models, we'll run a compatibility test; for open models we have pre-tested quant profiles.
[09:08] Maya: Great. Could you also confirm network egress constraints if we go Private on-prem? We need hairpin behavior inside our VPC.
[09:16] Jessie: Private on-prem avoids public egress; it runs inside your network and supports hairpin. That said, some telemetry export might need egress unless you host the telemetry collector. We'll clarify in the architecture diagram.
[09:29] Samir: Ok, let's surface the immediate next steps and owners. From our side: Samir will send pricing + pilot SOW; Jessie will run initial bench and share LLM latency matrix and LlamaIndex adapter examples; Claire will share required compliance docs and residency constraints; Maya/Omar will provision a test endpoint or allow Redwood bench to target a staging gateway.
[09:52] Maya: We'll aim to get Claire's list and a staging gateway endpoint by next week.
[09:57] Claire: Yes, I'll circulate the compliance checklist and stakeholders.
[10:01] Samir: Perfect — any last questions?
[10:04] Omar: Just one — if we run through a proxy what about per-user quotas? We want to enforce per-customer quotas even when calls are proxied by a service token.
[10:12] Jessie: You can pass the end-user id in a header and Redwood will attribute token usage to secondary keys for billing/quotas, but you need to use a header we recognize and enable attribution on your account. We'll include a short guide.
[10:26] Maya: That should work. Thanks everyone.
[10:29] Samir: Thanks — we'll follow up with the documents and SOW.

End of call.
